text: Iron atoms group into discrete four-cornered tetrahedral clusters that stand alone as a zero-dimensional unit, each metal centre having only a few near neighbours (a low coordination count).
Cobalt atoms pair up into upright two-atom dumbbells running along the vertical axis; these are isolated little struts with very few neighbours per atom.

Iron builds a dense, fully three-dimensional, topologically close-packed Frank-Kasper network of interpenetrating polyhedra with a large number of neighbours around every site, caging the rare-earth guests.
Each rare-earth atom sits at the centre of a twenty-vertex icosahedral shell of iron neighbours, a high-neighbour-count cage repeating through three dimensions.
Manganese and oxygen knit together into a three-dimensional framework of six-coordinate octahedra that share their corners throughout the structure.
Six-coordinate trigonal-prismatic pockets sit between the metal sheets, tying the layers into a three-dimensional framework.
Iron threads into one-dimensional zigzag chains; each atom bonds to just a couple of chain neighbours and the chains do not cross-link.
Cobalt atoms close into puckered rings that connect through the three-dimensional structure, with a moderate-to-large number of neighbours per atom.
Iron forms a flat kagome pattern of corner-sharing triangles within a single quasi-two-dimensional sheet, a moderate number of in-plane neighbours.
A flat square grid of iron atoms lies within a quasi-two-dimensional layer, each atom with a middling count of in-plane neighbours.
The metal atoms form a diffuse, percolating three-dimensional backbone with no single recognisable polyhedron, a generic close-knit network at moderate coordination.
Three-coordinate trigonal-pyramidal units assemble into an open framework where every centre has only a small number of neighbours.
Iron sits in compact triangular, three-fold environments that repeat to build a stiff three-dimensional framework at a moderate neighbour count.
Manganese and oxygen link head-to-tail into straight one-dimensional rows extending along a single axis, each centre bonded to few neighbours.
